target: services/flood_truth.py — resolve the address's council with lookup_lga so #892's absent-study scoping uses a signal that exists; plus lot-search hazard flags, the Tweed/Wollongong raster shipping path, and the flood calibration.
findings_summary: Measured first, and the measurement is why this change exists: ses_study_lga is null for 121 of 151 stored flood reports (80.1%), including 109 of 109 rows that were queried and fell outside every study extent — 100% of that bucket. It is not 'which council is this address in', it is 'which study matched', so it is null exactly when a missing study would matter and #892's scoping is close to inert. The replacement already exists: services/lga_lookup.py::lookup_lga(lat, lng, conn, address=None) resolves LGA from spatial_overlays layer_type='height' by ST_Contains and returns {'lga_name': None, ...} rather than raising when it fails. flood_truth.py already opens connections the same way — _get_conn() at lines 441, 800, 865 — and _query_ses_flood_study is the pattern to mirror: RealDictCursor, SET LOCAL statement_timeout, a typed null_result on failure. Schema confirmed: spatial_overlays holds layer_type='height' rows carrying lga_name, which is what lookup_lga reads; property_reports has twelve columns and no is_active, so no active-row filter applies to the census. Blast radius of the lot-search change checked before editing: no component renders a lot row's hazard flags — FilterPanel and ProspectorClient reference filters.heritage (already TriState), not the result rows — so the ?? false coercion was wrong but nothing displayed it, which bounds the fix as correct-but-low-impact rather than a live customer-facing repair.
